On the bullish side, one camp saw a refinery and fertilizer group set to benefit from tight fuel and nitrogen markets, with uninterrupted operations and M&A optionality. That Narrative pointed to a Fair Value of US$30, a price that reflected expectations for stronger margins from improved product mix and lower Renewable Identification Number obligations.

The bearish view focused on aging assets and energy transition pressure that could strain cash flows. That Narrative pointed to a Fair Value of US$19, built on concerns that stricter decarbonization policy, ESG driven capital limits, and rising maintenance needs would weigh on long term profitability and liquidity.

The hinge here was the path of earnings quality, not the share price. When you assess another refiner or fertilizer player, track whether higher sales translate into a smaller loss or a higher margin, then compare that with whatever profitability story you are being presented.
